unharnessed.meaning: Every instruction kept: three gallons, strain through muslin, overflow pipe, ten-gallon tank, two pet cocks, notch settings. Additions ("you'll blow your arse to kingdom come", "give you a hell of a whack") are colour on the original's warnings.
unharnessed.sense: Fits: "under its own steam", "the more grunt you get", "topped up", "Once the engine's properly loosened up" for limbered up.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Aussie plain speech ("make bloody sure", "dead sure", "beats hard water hands down"), with a couple of stock lines bolted on ("full stop").
unharnessed.register: Casual and clear but closer to level 3 than a level-5 yarn; long stretches are just plain paraphrase ("The system holds about three gallons."). Swearing ("bloody", "arse", "hell") within level 2.
unharnessed.tone: Still an instruction manual, with the cautions kept serious ("don't you dare, under any circumstances").
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Keep pouring water in till you're dead sure the radiator and the cylinder water jackets are both full."
unharnessed.essence: Plainly the 1919 Ford starting checklist, Q-and-A shape intact.

engine.meaning: Critical errors: "the gasoline tank may be rooted, knackered by openin' the pet cock" turns draining into wrecking; "How are Spark and Throttle Levers used, ya galah? Buggered if I know." and "Beats me." undercut the instructions.
engine.sense: "rooted, knackered" for drained, "stuffed, mate" for full, "a beaut plan": several wrong senses.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian bolt-ons: "Stone the flamin' crows", "Strewth", "Jeez Louise", "Oh, shit", "Fair fuckin' dinkum", "Well, I'll be buggered."; US "gasoline" and "carburetor" left.
engine.register: Heavy on exclamations but the body is the untouched original ("Upon receipt of the car see that a supply of medium light, high-grade gas engine oil"); swearing within level 2.
engine.tone: The careful manual is made flippant and ignorant: "Buggered if I know.", "no matter what some drongo reckons".
engine.flow: Broken joins: "Well, During the first few days", "gasoline'n air", "Anyway, under the steering wheel".
engine.essence: Under the noise the manual is there, but it no longer reads as instructions anyone could trust.

yarn.meaning: Every instruction kept with numbers and cross-references; additions are colour on the original ("it'll go up like a bonfire on cracker night", "that crank handle'll give your wrist a wallop").
yarn.sense: Exact: "chock-a-block" for full, "bungs up the little tubes", "Soon as the car rocks up" for upon receipt, "goin' flat out" for maximum speed.
yarn.authenticity: A real Aussie mechanic's voice: "get your mitts on", "be careful as", "quick smart", "suss out where they need to be".
yarn.register: A full level-5 yarn throughout, every section retold; swearing light ("make bloody sure", "flamin' volatile"), inside level 2.
yarn.tone: Still a careful how-to under the yarn: "And this is the big one: don't run the car under her own steam".
yarn.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Pour the oil in nice and slow till it runs out the top cock."
yarn.variety: Very varied idiom, though "she"/"her" for the car and dropped-g forms recur a lot.
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the Ford starting checklist, retold by a bush mechanic.

unharnessed.quote: Don't run the car under its own steam unless the water system's been filled, full stop.
unharnessed.original: It is important that the car should not be run under its own power unless the water circulating system has been filled.

unharnessed.quote: The system holds about three gallons.
unharnessed.original: The system will hold approximately three gallons.
unharnessed.why: Large plain stretches leave it lighter than the level-5 brief.
Keeps the US "gas" even after switching to petrol.

engine.quote: the gasoline tank may be rooted, knackered by openin' the pet cock
engine.original: The gasoline tank may be drained by opening the pet cock
engine.why: Says opening the cock wrecks the tank.

engine.quote: How are Spark and Throttle Levers used, ya galah? Buggered if I know.
engine.original: How are Spark and Throttle Levers used?
engine.why: Adds an insult and denies the knowledge the section then gives.

engine.quote: Where should these levers be when starting the Engine? Beats me.
engine.original: Where should these levers be when starting the Engine?

engine.why: "stuffed" means broken or exhausted, not filled.
Oath bolted onto a plain instruction.

yarn.quote: the little breather hole in the petrol cap
yarn.original: The small vent hole in the gasoline tank cap
yarn.why: "breather" also names the oil breather pipe; slight risk of confusion.

yarn.quote: the faster she runs and the more grunt ya get
yarn.why: "she"/"her" for the car is leaned on.

summaries.unharnessed: Accurate, natural and readable, but pitched lighter than level 5.
summaries.engine: Rule-engine noise over an untranslated manual, with an outright mistranslation of draining the tank.
summaries.yarn: A complete, natural level-5 retelling that stays a usable manual.
